cards.explanation: The answer is to the very end. John says, "…He loved them to the very end." Not halfway, friends, and not until it got hard. Whatever comes next that night, His love is already there.

The answer is the devil. John says "…the devil had already put into the heart of Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot, to betray Jesus." That's heavy, so I'll say it plainly and leave it there. Notice the word "already." The meal was underway, and this was already in Judas' heart.

The answer is True. John says Jesus knew "…that He had come from God and was returning to God." So He knows where He started and where He's headed. Keep that in mind, friends, because it makes what He does next even bigger.

The answer is basin. John says Jesus "…poured water into a basin and began to wash the disciples’ feet…" It's a plain, everyday tub for a plain, everyday job. And the One doing the job is anything but plain.

The answer is True. Jesus tells Peter, "You do not realize now what I am doing, but later you will understand." So Peter doesn't realize it yet, and Jesus promises that understanding is coming. Plenty of my batches made sense only after they came out of the oven.

The answer is that Peter says Jesus will never wash his feet. Peter tells Him, "Never shall You wash my feet!" Jesus just said understanding would come later, and Peter answers with a flat no. I think that's a bold thing to say to the Lord.

The answer is that Peter asks for his hands and head washed too. Peter says, "Then, Lord, not only my feet, but my hands and my head as well!" He heard "…you have no part with Me." and answered right away. He asks for more than just his feet.
The answer is False. Jesus says, "And you are clean, though not all of you." He doesn't call every disciple clean, friends. John explains why in the very next verse.

The answer is that He knew who would betray Him. John says, "For He knew who would betray Him." That is why Jesus said, "Not all of you are clean." Jesus isn't guessing here, because He knows. And He washed those feet anyway.
The answer is True. Jesus says, "You call Me Teacher and Lord, and rightly so, because I am." He doesn't wave the titles away, friends. He says they fit.

The answer is to wash one another's feet. Jesus says, "So if I, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also should wash one another’s feet." He doesn't stop at telling them what He did. He points them toward each other.

The answer is messenger. Jesus says, "…no servant is greater than his master, nor is a messenger greater than the one who sent him." Those two pairs sit side by side. And He opens it with "Truly, truly," so it's worth underlining.
The answer is False. Jesus says, "If you know these things, you will be blessed if you do them." Knowing alone isn't the promise, friends. It's the doing that comes with the blessing.
The answer is someone who shares His bread. Jesus quotes the Scripture: "The one who shares My bread has lifted up his heel against Me." (Psalm 41:9) That's close, and it's why this hurts to read.

The answer is so that they will believe. Jesus says, "I am telling you now before it happens, so that when it comes to pass, you will believe that I am He." He tells them first so that when it happens, they'll believe. He's thinking ahead for them.

The answer is the One who sent Him. Jesus says, "…whoever receives Me receives the One who sent Me." Receiving Jesus is tied right to the One who sent Him, friends. And it follows the line of the one He sends, too.
